context.title: Rich Toward God
context.summary: Jesus warns against hypocrisy and greed, tells of a rich fool who dies the night he plans bigger barns, urges trust instead of worry, and calls for servants ready for their master's return.
context.background: A man asks Jesus to settle an inheritance dispute (v. 13), a role often given to respected teachers. Jesus refuses and addresses the greed underneath. The weather sayings in vv. 54–55 fit the land: clouds from the west over the Mediterranean brought rain; a south wind from the desert brought heat.

customs.note: Men wore long robes and tucked them into the belt to move or work quickly. It means 'be ready for action.'

watchFor: The rich man talks only to himself: 'my barns… my goods… my soul' (vv. 17–19).
'Unto whomsoever much is given, of him shall be much required' (v. 48).

people.name: Jesus
people.also: Immanuel, Emmanuel, Messiah, Shiloh, Christ, Jesus Christ, Messias
people.summary: Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah”, the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament.

people.name: Holy Spirit
people.summary: The third Person of the adorable Trinity.

people.name: Solomon
people.summary: Peaceful, (Heb. Shelomoh), David’s second son by Bathsheba, i.e., the first after their legal marriage (2 Sam. 12). He was probably born about B.C. 1035 (1 Chr. 22:5; 29:1).

people.name: Simon
people.summary: Originally called Simon (=Simeon, i.e., “hearing”), a very common Jewish name in the New Testament. He was the son of Jona (Matt. 16:17). His mother is nowhere named in Scripture.
